label: EEA and Norway Grants
detail: Paid to 15 poorer EU member states. Norway funds roughly 97% of the two mechanisms combined; Poland was the largest recipient of the 2014-2021 period at EUR 809.3m
source: Norwegian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (norway.no); regjeringen.no

label: EU programme participation
detail: Horizon 2020, Erasmus+, Galileo, Copernicus and others. The fee is set by a GDP-based proportionality factor, 2.33% in 2022

label: Justice and home affairs / Schengen
detail: Single-year figure; the ministry does not publish an annual series for this line

label: Horizon Europe funding won
detail: Competitive research funding won by Norwegian institutions. Norway has taken 3.23% of total Horizon Europe funding against a government target of 2.8%
source: European Commission (Country Participation in the EU R&I Framework Programmes); Research Council of Norway

label: Horizon 2020 funding won
detail: Competitive research funding won by Norwegian institutions across the whole programme
source: European Commission (Country Participation in the EU R&I Framework Programmes)

label: Share of the EEA Grants
detail: Iceland's share of the EEA Financial Mechanism. Sources disagree between 3% and 4.2% depending on period and basis; no Icelandic government figure in euros was found
source: Norwegian MFA / European Parliament; EEA Grants Status Report 2022

label: Horizon Europe funding won
detail: Competitive research funding won by Icelandic institutions
source: European Commission (Country Participation in the EU R&I Framework Programmes)

label: Horizon 2020 funding won
detail: Competitive research funding won by Icelandic institutions across the whole programme
source: European Commission (Country Participation in the EU R&I Framework Programmes)

label: First cohesion contribution
detail: CHF 1.0bn to the ten 2004 entrants, CHF 257m added for Bulgaria and Romania, CHF 45m for Croatia. Projects ran to the end of 2024
source: Swiss Federal Department of Foreign Affairs (europa.eda.admin.ch)

label: Second Swiss contribution
detail: CHF 1.1bn cohesion to the 13 states that joined since 2004, plus CHF 200m for migration, which also reaches Greece and Italy
source: Swiss Federal Department of Foreign Affairs (europa.eda.admin.ch)

label: Interim annual payment
detail: Bridging payment from the end of 2024 until the new regular mechanism takes effect

label: Regular mechanism (planned)
detail: Agreed as part of the new package of agreements signed on 2 March 2026; not yet ratified

label: National research funding during exclusion
detail: Not an EU flow. Swiss federal money spent replacing Horizon Europe access after Switzerland was made a non-associated third country
source: Swiss State Secretariat for Education Research and Innovation (SBFI)

label: European Research Council grants won
detail: First year back inside Horizon Europe after re-association
